messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/chat/stream (region: us-west-2). Current p99=4.9s (SLO=2.0s). Trigger: latency-slo-p99-violation. Link: https://dash.redwood/alerts/3971112222

alice: got paged. seeing streaming stalls reported by the agent. starting triage.

ben: i pulled the traces — annotation shows a big stall inside gpu-infer-step around KV cache access. p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~4.9s.

carla: @alice @ben oncall? i'm stepping in for infra handoff in 5.

alice: handing to carla — forwarding running checklist. main risk: continued customer P99 breaches and retries.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-397111 (priority: P1). Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-degradation-streaming.

carla: summary for execs: many streaming sessions experienced tail stalls, visible as stuck chunks for ~3-6s before resume. intermittent across 3 nodes in gw-pool-9. customers: 3 high-traffic tenants with active sessions.

matt: customer-impact: two customers reported slow responses and elevated error-rate (500s from streaming timeouts). Support alerted them and offered workarounds.

devin: adding routing mitigation: i'll enable model-fallback to smaller-quantized variant for gw-pool-9 and route new sessions to pool-11. this should lower latency for new requests.

ben: logs from one node (gpu-node-9a) show correctable ECC counts spiking:
```
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z gpu0 ecc_correctable=12
2026-03-15T10:02:17Z gpu0 ecc_correctable=35
2026-03-15T10:02:23Z gpu0 thermal=82C throttle=partial
2026-03-15T10:02:29Z infer_step stall=3721ms
```

alice: thermal creeping up + ECC flurry. looks like hardware-level instability causing occasional long stalls in the kernel.

carla: can we cordon/drain the affected nodes without causing mass failover? recommend draining gpu-node-9a then incrementally offload.

devin: running `infractl drain gpu-node-9a --grace=30s --skip-live-migrations` to avoid streaming stalls during migration.

ben: note: draining will push more traffic to pool-11 which has lower capacity. will enable temporary autoscale bump and the fallback.

matt: notifying impacted customers now with ETA ~15-25m. offering to move active sessions to hosted fallback if needed.

incident-bot: paging on-call SRE: carla (escalation path triggered).

carla: drain started. monitoring token-level latency and drop rates.

alice: while drain runs, enable cache-prefix-hint to reduce KV hits for hot prompts on pool-11: `service-config set cache_hint=prefix-hot --target=pool-11`

ben: good idea. applying that now.

devin: autoscale +1 node in pool-11, model-fallback enabled, cache hints live.

carla: drain completed for gpu-node-9a. observed ~20s of increased tail as sessions moved, then p99 dropped to ~2.1s. still slightly above SLO.

ben: observed another node gpu-node-9b showing intermittent ECC correctables but not as spiky as 9a. tracking both. kernel vendor logs show occasional PCI link retries — possible flaky riser or power delivery.

matt: updated customers: 'we rerouted traffic and are replacing a flaky accelerator; expect normal performance in ~1hr. we'll follow up when resolved.' response: :thumbsup: from one customer, another asked for root cause update.

carla: next actions: open hardware vendor ticket for nodes 9a/9b, schedule hot-swap. continue monitoring p99. set rollback to original pool when stable.

alice: running longer tail-eval against the regression set to ensure quality didn't regress after fallback model. initial checks ok.

ben: p99 now holding ~1.9s for last 10m; p95 ~0.9s. streaming stall rate down to 0.2% of sessions (was 3.1%).

devin: i'll leave fallback in place for 30m and then gradually shift traffic back. will keep autoscale for 1hr.

carla: thanks team. converting to postmortem tracking: INC-2026-397111. assigning owners: hardware ticket (ben), routing/fallback lessons (devin), customer comms (matt), postmortem write-up (alice).

incident-bot: Incident severity lowered to P2 (monitoring) — no active paging. Links: https://dash.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-397111

matt: closing customer loop: sent RCA note draft; waiting on hardware vendor ETA.

alice: will start postmortem draft once vendor confirms root cause.

carla: closing this thread for paging, keep channel for updates. great response — saved noisy customer escalations. :tada:
